root_cause.text: On UP kernels, spin_trylock() is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds regardless of lock state, allowing kmalloc_nolock() called from NMI context to re-enter the slab allocator and acquire locks already held by the interrupted context, corrupting slab state.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an early NULL return for NMI context on UP kernels with the comment "On UP, spin_trylock() always succeeds even when it is locked". The CVE description explicitly states that on UP kernels (!CONFIG_SMP), spin_trylock() is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds, which causes kmalloc_nolock() to re-enter and acquire n->list_lock that the interrupted context is already holding, leading to slab state corruption.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add NMI context check for UP kernels to prevent unsafe memory allocation when spin_trylock() semantics cannot guarantee lock safety.
intent_record.what: Added a new guard clause that returns NULL when CONFIG_SMP is disabled (UP kernel) and the code is executing in NMI context, with an explanatory comment about spin_trylock() behavior on UP systems.
intent_record.how: This prevents kmalloc_nolock_noprof from attempting allocation in NMI context on single-processor (UP) kernels. On UP systems, spin_trylock() always succeeds regardless of lock state, which could cause issues if memory allocation is attempted while a lock is held in NMI context. The guard ensures safe behavior by bailing out early in this problematic scenario.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by adding an NMI context check for UP kernels. This prevents kmalloc_nolock() from being called in NMI context where spin_trylock() cannot guarantee lock safety, thus avoiding the slab allocator re-entry and lock corruption described in the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This condition only checks for NMI/hardirq context when CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT is enabled. On UP kernels without PREEMPT_RT, this check is bypassed, allowing kmalloc_nolock() to proceed unsafely. Since spin_trylock() is a no-op on UP kernels, the function can re-enter the slab allocator from NMI context and corrupt slab state. The vulnerability exists because the NMI check is gated behind CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT instead of being applied to all UP kernels where spin_trylock() cannot provide lock safety guarantees.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition gates the NMI/hardirq safety check behind CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT, which is incorrect. On UP kernels without PREEMPT_RT enabled, spin_trylock() is a no-op that always succeeds, making it unsafe to call kmalloc_nolock() from NMI context. The condition should check for NMI/hardirq context on all UP kernels (where spin_trylock() cannot guarantee lock safety), not just when PREEMPT_RT is enabled. This allows kmalloc_nolock() to re-enter the slab allocator from NMI context on vanilla UP kernels, corrupting slab state.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit removes critical protection against NMI reentrancy in kmalloc_nolock(). Specifically: (1) Lines 5215-5216 remove the check `if (!in_nmi() || !local_lock_is_locked(&s->cpu_slab->lock))` that previously prevented calling __slab_alloc_node() from NMI context when the lock was already held by interrupted code. This check was crucial because on UP kernels, spin_trylock() is a no-op. (2) The comment at lines 5216-5223 explaining the NMI safety is deleted, removing the explanation of why the conditional call was necessary. (3) Line 5220 now unconditionally calls `ret = __slab_alloc_node(s, alloc_gfp, node, _RET_IP_, size)` without the NMI guard. This allows kmalloc_nolock() invoked from NMI context to re-enter slab allocator code and potentially re-acquire locks already held by the interrupted context, causing slab state corruption. The fix (preventing this unconditional call on UP kernels in NMI) is not present in this version.
